name: Chris O'Malley

tenures.source: his own held bio card, "Superstar bio: Chris O'Malley" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/bio-chris-omalley.html); staged on the 27 April 2008 War Games (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html) and the 20 January 2013 closing show, "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: At 20113 he drew with Robert Garland in the Breakthrough Tournament's own opening round, then forfeited his long-held Intercontinental Championship for a slot in the closing show's own main event — where he pinned Garland to become GWF's final Champion.

caption: GWF's own "Golden Standard," Chris O'Malley fought Mark Madison across two Rise and Fall main events for the International Xtreme Championship — 2007's own Feud of the Year, per the fed's own account — and closed the promotion's own history as its last GWF Champion.

name: The Reprobate

tenures.style: An old-school heel with a modern evil twist — an ultimate slacker who leans on managers and tag partners.
tenures.source: his own held bio card, "Superstar bio: The Reprobate" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/bio-the-reprobate.html); staged on the 27 March 2009 FNB Reunion show and the 20 January 2013 closing show, "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-fnb-reunion-2009-03-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: Won the FNB Reunion's own US Title tournament to the final before losing there to Star-Man; challenged Star-Man for the US title again at 20113 and lost again. Reclaimed the vacant Hardcore Championship backstage at 20113 and retained it that same night over Roc Anderson.

caption: An old-school heel out of New York who held the GWF Interbrand Championship for eight months running into March 2009 and reclaimed the Hardcore Championship at the fed's own closing show, per his own bio card and the surviving record.

name: The Soul of Philly

tenures.source: his own held sign-up card, "Sign-up card: The Soul of Philly TJ" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/bio-the-soul-of-philly.html)
tenures.note: A March 2009 debut sign-up card, filed during GWF's own reunion tour; no reign or result yet on record. His own submitted sample RP is explicitly a writing sample set in an outside continuity ("WWER"), not a GWF appearance, and is not structured as one.

caption: A March 2009 sign-up out of Philadelphia, styled after a man who had finally made peace with his own past — no reign or result yet on the record.

name: SheltonSplash

tenures.role: GWF's own founder and site admin, also a wrestler and Cataclysm's own leader
tenures.source: the board's own front matter throughout; staged on the 27 April 2008 War Games, the 5 April 2009 promo "The Living Fairytale," and the 20 January 2013 closing show "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/rp-the-living-fairytale.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: Founded GWF in 2006 and wrote/booked its own closing show. Won the GWF Championship at Valentine's Vengeance 2008, later lost it to Don Cicinni in a match recovered only as a flashback. Also lost the GWF Tag Team Championship, partnered with Kevin McAuliffe, to XO Malone and Damian DeNiro's Movement, again recovered only as a flashback. At 20113 he took the vacated Intercontinental Championship for himself without a match, was overruled, and was eliminated first from the resulting five-way; also fought Ken Davidson to a double-knockout draw off a ladder through some production crates.

caption: GWF's own founder, site admin and closing-show booker — "Your Friend, Your Pal, Your Hated Nemesis, Your Boss, Your Creator," in his own words, signing off the fed for good on 20 January 2013.

name: Dave Shadow

tenures.role: GWF owner and wrestler, half of the tag team Neo-Evolution with Kevin McAuliffe
tenures.source: staged on the 27 June 2008 Mini FNB main event, the 27 April 2008 War Games, and the 20 January 2013 closing show "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/mini-fnb.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: Beat Damian DeNiro in a non-title match on 27 June 2008; on the winning Numbered Toast/Neo-Evolution side of the 27 April 2008 War Games. At 20113 he beat Danny Mainer, lost to Chris O'Malley by disqualification (a Bryan Daniels low blow), and lost Neo-Evolution's own GWF Tag Team Championship to Danny Mainer and Bryan Daniels.

caption: GWF's own owner, once stripped Cataclysm of the Tag Team Championship as its authority figure and fought as one half of Neo-Evolution alongside Kevin McAuliffe.

name: "Metal" Michael Toaster

tenures.role: GWF board admin and wrestler, half of the tag team Numbered Toast with The Number 4
tenures.source: the board's own front matter throughout; staged on the 27 April 2008 War Games, the abandoned draft "The original Toaster vs. Number 4 match," and the 20 January 2013 closing show "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/toaster-vs-number-4.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: Debuted as "Toast Hogan," a Hulk Hogan-parody gimmick and GWF Cruiserweight Champion, during the 2006 Food Division craze, before dropping the gimmick to win the World, US and Tag Team Championships as Michael Toaster (per the fed's own 28 July 2008 Hall of Shame retrospective). Won the GWF Championship from James Murphy, undated, before losing it to Chris O'Malley at Locked N' Loaded 2007. Defeated tag partner-turned-rival The Number 4 in a Loser Leaves GWF match, forcing Number 4 out of GWF for roughly eight months (per Number 4's own March 2009 dialogue) — the served draft of this match was itself superseded by a longer final version never captured. Won the 20113 Money in the Bank ladder match, then lost the closing show's own GWF Championship match to Chris O'Malley; briefly returned to the ring as "Toast Hogan" the same night to attack T-Dog Tomasio.

caption: GWF board admin and one-time GWF Champion who began as the Hulk Hogan-parody "Toast Hogan," won the fed's own final Money in the Bank ladder match, and made a one-night-only return to the Toast Hogan gimmick at the closing show.

name: The Number 4

tenures.role: wrestler, former Saturday Night Dogfight general manager, later the 2009 reunion tour's own promoter/owner; half of the tag team Numbered Toast with Michael Toaster
tenures.source: staged on the 27 April 2008 War Games, the abandoned draft "The original Toaster vs. Number 4 match," the 27 March 2009 FNB Reunion show, and the 20 January 2013 closing show "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/toaster-vs-number-4.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-fnb-reunion-2009-03-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: Lost a Loser Leaves GWF match to former tag partner Michael Toaster (result confirmed by his own 2009 dialogue; the served written match is an abandoned, superseded draft). Returned roughly eight months later as the 2009 reunion tour's own promoter. Never pinned or made to submit in his own five-year-plus GWF career, per the fed's own 20113 commentary, until the closing show's own Bathroom Stall Brawl, where he was stopped by referee decision against Joseph Appice.

caption: GWF's own reunion-tour promoter — never pinned or forced to submit in over five years, until the closing show's own Bathroom Stall Brawl finally stopped him.

name: Damian DeNiro

tenures.role: wrestler, GWF United States Champion, one half of The Movement with XO Malone
tenures.source: staged on the 27 June 2008 Mini FNB main event, the 27 April 2008 War Games (billed "Damian DeVil"), and the 5 April 2009 promo "The Living Fairytale" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/mini-fnb.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/rp-the-living-fairytale.html)
tenures.note: Posts under both "Damian DeNiro" and "Damian DeVil," the same board account (Member No. 9, same custom title, "HE'S WATCHING YOU EVERYWHERE YOU TURN!") across documents. Lost to Dave Shadow in a non-title match on 27 June 2008. Won a three-way Survival Success qualifier over Don Cicinni and Debolt Dragonsbane at the 27 April 2008 War Games card. Won the GWF Tag Team Championship, partnered with XO Malone as The Movement, over SheltonSplash and Kevin McAuliffe in a match recovered only as a flashback clip.

caption: Half of XO Malone's own Movement stable and a former GWF United States Champion, billed under two spellings of his own name across the surviving record.

name: XO Malone

tenures.role: wrestler, leader of the stable The Movement, later Co-Cruiserweight Champion
tenures.source: staged on the 27 June 2008 Mini FNB main event, the 27 March 2009 FNB Reunion show, the 5 April 2009 promo "The Living Fairytale," and the 20 January 2013 closing show "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/mini-fnb.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-fnb-reunion-2009-03-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/rp-the-living-fairytale.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: Interfered, with a masked ally billed as "Sinister Minster," in a June 2008 title match on behalf of The Movement. Won the GWF Tag Team Championship alongside Damian DeNiro, a reign recovered only as a flashback. Lost to The Reprobate in the FNB Reunion's own US Title tournament. At 20113, became Co-Cruiserweight Champion with Debolt Dragonsbane before the belt was unified into the International Xtreme Championship the same night.

caption: Leader of the stable The Movement and, briefly, GWF's own Co-Cruiserweight Champion at the promotion's very last show.

name: Kevin McAuliffe

tenures.role: wrestler, one half of the tag team Neo-Evolution with Dave Shadow
tenures.source: staged on the 27 April 2008 War Games, the 27 March 2009 FNB Reunion show, and the 20 January 2013 closing show "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-fnb-reunion-2009-03-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: On the winning Numbered Toast/Neo-Evolution side of the 27 April 2008 War Games. Beat James Murphy at the FNB Reunion tournament, then was attacked with a cricket bat by Murphy after the match and lost his semifinal to The Reprobate as a result. First ever winner of the Survival Success match, per the fed's own 20113 commentary (undated, not independently structured). At 20113 he beat Bryan Daniels, lost to Chris Williams (Danny Mainer interference), reached the Money in the Bank ladder match's own final two, and lost the GWF Tag Team Championship alongside Dave Shadow.

caption: One half of Neo-Evolution alongside Dave Shadow and the first ever winner of GWF's own Survival Success match, per the fed's own account.

name: James Murphy

tenures.role: wrestler, GWF Champion and Cataclysm member
tenures.source: his own bio referenced within Chris O'Malley's held bio card; staged on the 27 June 2008 Mini FNB main event, the 27 April 2008 War Games, and the 27 March 2009 FNB Reunion show (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/bio-chris-omalley.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/mini-fnb.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-fnb-reunion-2009-03-27.html)
tenures.note: Held the GWF Championship before losing it to Michael Toaster, undated. Lost to AT Fire in a non-title match on 27 June 2008, then attacked special referee Ken Davidson afterward. On the losing Cataclysm side of the 27 April 2008 War Games. Lost to Kevin McAuliffe at the FNB Reunion tournament, then attacked him with a cricket bat after the bell.

caption: A former GWF Champion and Cataclysm member whose cricket bat became his own trademark weapon of choice outside the referee's sight.

name: AT Fire

tenures.role: wrestler, GWF Hall of Famer
tenures.source: staged on the 27 June 2008 Mini FNB main event (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/mini-fnb.html)
tenures.note: Beat James Murphy in a non-title match on 27 June 2008, seconded to the ring by Robert Garland.

caption: A GWF Hall of Famer who beat former champion James Murphy in a June 2008 special attraction, seconded to the ring by Robert Garland.

name: Ken Davidson

tenures.role: wrestler and occasional special referee
tenures.source: staged on the 27 June 2008 Mini FNB main event, the 27 March 2009 FNB Reunion show, and the 20 January 2013 closing show "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/mini-fnb.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-fnb-reunion-2009-03-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: Served as special referee for the AT Fire/James Murphy main event on 27 June 2008, then was attacked by Murphy after the bell. Lost to Jeff Maximus in the FNB Reunion's own tournament opener. His own 20113 promo claims a former Intercontinental Championship reign taken from SheltonSplash and a spoiled Money in the Bank opportunity, neither independently dated or structured. Fought SheltonSplash to a double-knockout draw at 20113, both men falling off a ladder through production crates.

caption: A wrestler and occasional special referee whose own history with SheltonSplash — a taken Intercontinental title, a spoiled Money in the Bank shot — boiled over into a double-knockout brawl at the fed's own closing show.

name: Robert Garland

tenures.role: wrestler and one-time special referee, later billed as an incarcerated convict allowed out only for his own matches
tenures.source: staged on the 27 June 2008 Mini FNB main event, the 27 April 2008 War Games, the 27 March 2009 FNB Reunion show, and the 20 January 2013 closing show "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/mini-fnb.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-fnb-reunion-2009-03-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: Seconded AT Fire to the ring and served as the War Games' own special referee on 27 April 2008. Lost to Star-Man in the FNB Reunion's own tournament opener. At 20113, drew with Chris O'Malley (a bloody 20-minute time-limit draw), then beat The Reprobate and won a triple-threat final over Chris Williams and Chris O'Malley to become GWF's only Breakthrough Champion — which also earned him a spot in the closing show's own GWF Championship match, which he lost.

caption: A former GWF World Champion billed at the closing show as a shackled convict allowed out of prison only to defend his own record — and did, becoming GWF's only Breakthrough Champion.

name: Star-Man

tenures.source: staged on the 27 March 2009 FNB Reunion show and the 20 January 2013 closing show "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-fnb-reunion-2009-03-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: Won the FNB Reunion's own eight-man US Title tournament as the field's own least experienced entrant, beating Robert Garland, Jeff Maximus and The Reprobate in succession. Retained the belt against The Reprobate again at 20113 in a hardcore rules match.

tenures.source: staged on the 20 January 2013 closing show "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: Billed a former GWF United States Champion and two-time PWA World Heavyweight Champion. Lost a bloody Hardcore Championship challenge to The Reprobate, kicked low after seemingly finishing him with the Falling Star.

caption: GWF's own least-experienced tournament entrant in March 2009, who beat three former champions in one night to become United States Champion and never lost the belt.

name: Jeff Maximus

tenures.source: staged on the 27 April 2008 SNS card, the 27 March 2009 FNB Reunion show, and the 20 January 2013 closing show "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-fnb-reunion-2009-03-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: Lost to Nicholas Zaltren in a Survival Success entry-number qualifier on 27 April 2008. Beat Ken Davidson at the FNB Reunion tournament, then lost the final to Star-Man. At 20113 his match with Nitro Nick ended in a double disqualification, and he was eliminated from the Money in the Bank ladder match by Nitro Nick's own Nitro Driver.

caption: A recurring GWF mid-carder whose 27 March 2009 loss to a debuting Star-Man in the US Title tournament final capped a night of near-misses.

name: Nicholas Zaltren

tenures.source: staged on the 27 April 2008 SNS card (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html)
tenures.note: Beat Jeff Maximus in a Survival Success entry-number qualifier, earning the match's own #20 spot.

caption: Earned the coveted #20 Survival Success entry with a single-knee facebuster win over Jeff Maximus on 27 April 2008.

name: Falcon McKenzie

tenures.source: staged on the 27 April 2008 SNS card (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html)
tenures.note: Retained the GWF International Xtreme Championship over Michael Smart in a bloody hardcore rules defense, using a fire extinguisher, a sledgehammer, a ladder and barbed wire before finishing him with the belt itself.

caption: GWF International Xtreme Champion who retained the belt over a fan-turned-heel Michael Smart in a bloody 27 April 2008 hardcore defense.

name: Michael Smart

tenures.source: staged on the 27 April 2008 SNS card and the 20 January 2013 closing show "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: Turned on the fans that had helped him win the International Xtreme Championship and lost his own challenge for it back on 27 April 2008. At 20113, entered as Sunday Brunch Heavyweight-Interbrand Champion on a technicality, lost his opening round to Chris Williams, then outlasted every reigning champion in the building to become GWF's only Champion of Champions.

caption: A fan favorite turned heel in his own failed International Xtreme title challenge, who nonetheless outlasted every reigning champion in the building to become GWF's only Champion of Champions.

name: Don Cicinni

identity.note: Aka collision on "The Don" with cwfpro's own cwfpro-the-don, and a name-shape collision with wwa's own don-valentino-wwa — no crossover evidence links any of the three; both mob-boss-styled ring names landed on independently, per THE PERFECTION WAVE's aka-collision guard.

tenures.role: wrestler, GWF Champion and, later, Cataclysm member
tenures.source: staged on the 27 April 2008 War Games' own preceding card, referenced in Chris O'Malley's own held bio card, and staged in the 5 April 2009 promo "The Living Fairytale" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/bio-chris-omalley.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/rp-the-living-fairytale.html)
tenures.note: Lost a three-way Survival Success qualifier to Damian DeVil on 27 April 2008, despite big-booting his own opponent Debolt Dragonsbane. Joined Cataclysm at Rise and Fall III, per Chris O'Malley's own bio card. Won the GWF Championship from SheltonSplash, needing three Omerta superkicks — recovered only as a flashback clip in a later promo.

caption: A former GWF Champion and Cataclysm member whose title win over SheltonSplash needed three superkicks and survives only as a flashback.

name: Debolt Dragonsbane

tenures.source: staged on the 27 April 2008 War Games' own preceding card and the 20 January 2013 closing show "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: Pinned in a three-way Survival Success qualifier by Damian DeVil on 27 April 2008. Became Co-Cruiserweight Champion with XO Malone at 20113, before the belt was unified into the International Xtreme Championship the same night.

caption: GWF's own Co-Cruiserweight Champion for one night, sharing the belt with XO Malone before it was folded into the International Xtreme Championship.

name: Bryan Daniels

tenures.source: staged on the 27 April 2008 War Games and the 20 January 2013 closing show "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: On the losing Cataclysm-allied side of the 27 April 2008 War Games. At 20113 he lost his opening round to Kevin McAuliffe, briefly grabbed the Money in the Bank briefcase before being stopped, and won the GWF Tag Team Championship alongside Danny Mainer.

caption: "The Main Event," whose four years away only sweetened his welcome back at GWF's own closing show, where he won the Tag Team Championship with Danny Mainer.

name: Chris Williams

identity.note: Decorated-aka near-matches on a common real-world name, unrelated wings, no crossover evidence — a generic name landed on independently, not a collision.

tenures.source: staged on the 27 April 2008 War Games and the 20 January 2013 closing show "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: On the winning Numbered Toast/Neo-Evolution side of the 27 April 2008 War Games. At 20113 he beat Michael Smart, beat Kevin McAuliffe with Danny Mainer's help, lost the Breakthrough Tournament final to Robert Garland, and won the vacant Intercontinental Championship in a five-way elimination match to become its own final champion.

caption: GWF's own final Intercontinental Champion, crowned in a five-way elimination match on the fed's own closing night.

name: John Beanshaw Wrathfield

tenures.role: wrestler, GWF Hall of Famer, posts under the account "Wrathbeans"
tenures.source: the fed's own 28 July 2008 Hall of Shame retrospective; staged in the 27 March 2009 FNB Reunion show's own backstage segment; billed for the 4 April 2009 SND card (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/hos-induction-7-28-08.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-fnb-reunion-2009-03-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-snd-card-2009-04-04.html)
tenures.note: Lost to fellow Spirit Squad opponent Wolfenstein by countout in GWF's earliest days, then won the GWF Tag Team Championship alongside Wolfenstein as the Billionaires Club — no date recovered for either. Confronted The Number 4 on his own reunion-tour return, demanding respect for GWF's absent legends. Billed against Chris O'Malley for the Intercontinental Championship on the 4 April 2009 SND card; that show's own results were never captured.

caption: A GWF Hall of Famer and former Tag Team Champion as one half of the Billionaires Club, who returned for the 2009 reunion tour to defend GWF's own absent legends.

name: Mark Madison

tenures.role: wrestler, former International Xtreme and Hardcore Champion, posts under the account "The Real Mark Madison"
tenures.source: referenced across Chris O'Malley's own held bio card and the fed's own 28 July 2008 Hall of Shame retrospective; billed for the 4 April 2009 SND card (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/bio-chris-omalley.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/hos-induction-7-28-08.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-snd-card-2009-04-04.html)
tenures.note: Debuted as "The Underbaker," a Ministry of Darkbread/Food Division-era gimmick, before a lengthy International Xtreme Championship feud with Chris O'Malley — a Basket Match at GWF's first pay-per-view, then title matches at the first two Rise and Fall shows, 2007's own Feud of the Year per the fed's own account. A returning-legend billed IX title challenge against Baron Trotter on the 4 April 2009 SND card was never captured with a result.

caption: Chris O'Malley's own longtime rival for the International Xtreme Championship, dating back to his early "Underbaker" gimmick — 2007's own Feud of the Year, per the fed's own account.

name: Baron Trotter

tenures.role: wrestler, GWF International Xtreme Champion
tenures.source: named as champion in the 27 March 2009 Power 10 column; billed for the 4 April 2009 SND card; staged on the 20 January 2013 closing show "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/power-10-2009-03-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-snd-card-2009-04-04.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: Held the International Xtreme Championship into the 2009 reunion tour; a billed 4 April 2009 defense against a returning Mark Madison was never captured with a result. At 20113 he interrupted and ended the Cruiserweight Championship match, then won a triple threat over XO Malone and Debolt Dragonsbane to become the Undisputed GWF International Xtreme Champion, and reached the closing show's own Money in the Bank ladder match.

caption: GWF's own final Undisputed International Xtreme Champion, unifying the belt with the Cruiserweight Championship on the promotion's very last night.

name: Danny Mainer

tenures.source: staged on the 20 January 2013 closing show "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: Remembered by the fed's own commentary for staging his own kayfabe death rather than accept being held down the card by then-owner Dave Shadow. At 20113 he lost his opening round to Dave Shadow, repeatedly interfered against Chris Williams and Chris O'Malley on Bryan Daniels's behalf, and won the GWF Tag Team Championship alongside Bryan Daniels after his own manager, Jessica, delivered a ringside low blow.

caption: Once faked his own death rather than stay held down the GWF card, and returned in 2013 to win the Tag Team Championship alongside Bryan Daniels.

name: Nitro Nick

tenures.role: wrestler, a former GWF Tag Team Champion per the fed's own 20113 commentary (partner and dates not independently recovered)
tenures.source: staged on the 20 January 2013 closing show "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: His match with Jeff Maximus ended in a double disqualification. In the Money in the Bank ladder match he lifted the 330-pound Baron Trotter off the mat before Toaster broke it up, then eliminated Jeff Maximus with a Nitro Driver off the ladder before losing the case to Michael Toaster.

caption: A returning former GWF Tag Team Champion who hoisted a 330-pound Baron Trotter clean off the mat in the closing show's own Money in the Bank ladder match.

name: Joseph Appice

tenures.role: guest wrestler, billed a former PWA World Interbrand Champion
tenures.source: staged on the 20 January 2013 closing show "20113," a guest entrant in the Bathroom Stall Brawl (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: The final two in a multi-man hardcore elimination brawl, dropping The Number 4 through a bathtub off a toilet and a mirror for a referee-decision win, only for T-Dog Tomasio to ambush and pin him moments later, awarded the match instead.

caption: A guest from outside GWF whose Bathroom Stall Brawl win — earned dropping The Number 4 through a bathtub — lasted only until T-Dog Tomasio's own post-match ambush.

name: T-Dog Tomasio

tenures.role: wrestler, a recurring rival of GWF's own former developmental territory EVE
tenures.source: staged on the 20 January 2013 closing show "20113" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: Remembered by the fed's own commentary for repeatedly ruining EVE shows. Spent most of the Bathroom Stall Brawl hidden in a bathtub outside the ring before ambushing declared winner Joseph Appice with two low blows and a Stunner to be awarded the match instead — before Michael Toaster, briefly returning as "Toast Hogan," beat him down after the fact.

caption: Won the closing show's own Bathroom Stall Brawl by hiding in a bathtub for most of the match and ambushing its already-declared winner — and got a beatdown from a returning Toast Hogan for his trouble.

name: Christina Hernandez

tenures.role: The Reprobate's own manager
tenures.source: The Reprobate's own held bio card; staged on the 27 March 2009 FNB Reunion show; billed for a shark-cage stipulation on the 4 April 2009 SND card (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/bio-the-reprobate.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-fnb-reunion-2009-03-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-snd-card-2009-04-04.html)
tenures.note: Interfered with two steel chairs to help The Reprobate beat XO in the FNB Reunion tournament, and again low-blowed the referee in the tournament final. Billed to be locked in a shark cage at ringside for The Reprobate's own 4 April 2009 US Title challenge; that show's own results were never captured.

caption: The Reprobate's own manager, whose ringside interference — steel chairs, a low-blowed referee — was as much a part of his tournament run as his own offense.

name: G-Ziss

tenures.role: wrestler, a religious-powerhouse gimmick managed by a televangelist, The Reverend
tenures.source: briefly worked GWF in 2006, per the fed's own 28 March 2009 GWF Insider column reporting his in-story death; staged in the 20 January 2013 closing show's own Bathroom Stall Brawl (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/gwf-insider-reunion-edition.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html)
tenures.note: The fed's own 28 March 2009 GWF Insider column reported his in-story death, age 37, cause undetermined, days earlier. Returned, framed as a tribute cameo, for the closing show's own Bathroom Stall Brawl, where he was pinned by Eve Eve after a botched top-rope suplex attempt.
